requirements.requirement: All existing content under /srv/inventory is owned by inventorysvc.
requirements.summary: Final and post-restart observations show both directories and both files owned by inventorysvc with group inventory-readers.

requirements.requirement: The existing data is readable by inventory-readers and inaccessible to other users.
requirements.summary: Directories have mode 750 and files mode 640 with inventory-readers as group. Direct tests demonstrate group read access while unaffiliated users cannot read files or traverse the top-level directory, including after restart.
The same two prepared files remain present, and their SHA-256 hashes match the authored baseline before repair, after repair, and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct metadata, checksum, and access-behavior evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, the restart was acknowledged, a different boot identity was observed and independently corroborated, and services, data, permissions, and access behavior recovered successfully.
limitations: Direct behavioral access tests sampled config.json before restart and records.csv after restart rather than testing every file under each identity; complete metadata and ACL listings nevertheless cover all preserved entries.
No cluster state was applicable because the managed topology contains only the single standalone node.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the missing service identity and reader group, changing ownership, and tightening modes directly established the required outcome (cmd-18736619cfef480f). The scheduled restart was required by the provider evidence protocol and was followed by complete recovery validation (cmd-47ac43e1b2a6447a, cmd-eb9e9ee1f54d4c36, cmd-20dc52b9bf734d35). Lifecycle evidence shows no failed services, damaged package state, new exposure, or abnormal temporary residue after execution.
